NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: `stat` device/inode can be recycled after `unlink`, so a comparison of a recorded pair against a re-read path cannot tell an object from a same-path replacement on a filesystem that recycles inode numbers. The repair therefore pins identity to the opened object: open once, record the pair with `fstat` of that handle, read the lock's ownership bytes from the same handle, and hold the handle until the destructive call. An open handle keeps the observed inode allocated, so a replacement cannot receive that number and the comparison becomes sound. `fstat` binding closes the separate-path gap that let an implementation open one object and record another after a rename, or read `readFileSync(path)` and `statSync(path)` from two different lock files. When the handle cannot be obtained the operation preserves and refuses with a named diagnostic and never substitutes the unpinned comparison, because that comparison is exactly the deletion the Linux CI observed. The ordinary `spec new` mint and handled cleanup must still succeed on a supported platform, Windows included; the Windows job is the only place a Windows platform claim is taken from. The ext4 measurements below were taken on 2026-09-23 on Linux with Bun 1.3.14; the release-owner probes name their Bun version separately. The implementation authority independently confirmed in a separate disposable ext4 mount that unpinned file and directory replacements reused an inode 100/100 times each, versus 0/100 with the old object open. A release-owner gap was found after the `C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-2-D4F54467` approval: `writeSpecNew` and the supersede transaction each discarded a pinned candidate without releasing it, so a long-running process leaked one descriptor per successful mint or transaction. That gap is closed in the committed tree this bundle adopts (`writeSpecNew` releases at `src/grace-generate.ts:441`; the transaction releases at `src/gates/ledger.ts:1715` on success and closes through `cleanupCandidate` at `:1740` on a post-mint failure). The owner probes below are prototype measurements of the pre-repair shape; the normative criteria re-validate the committed repair. **Governance supersede and committed-code adoption.** This successor is not a second implementation. The earlier repair tasks landed the code on `c-supersede-membership`; those commits remain in history and this bundle adopts them. Two supersede steps preceded it. `C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-2-D4F54467` (archived, superseded) was superseded because its approved plan promised, in its T-004 criterion, that the implementation authority would record the full GitHub Actions **job URL** in the bundle's evidence. A GitHub Actions run or job link embeds the repository owner's account handle in its path, which the repository's public-content rule forbids in any surface, and the shipped writer surfaces cannot carry it URL-free: the cursor subcommand set has no external-job URL field, and `gate verdict --note` writes free text into `run-ledger.xml`, itself a committed surface. An approved plan is immutable, so the repair was `C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-3-7EB3B2C3`, whose bounded change is a **positive** evidence record, not merely a negative URL filter: the implementation authority — not the executor, whose prose here is input only — independently inspects the remote run through the authenticated GitHub API/CLI and commits a bundle-local `ci-evidence.json` sidecar (schemaVersion `1.0.0`) naming the exact candidate SHA, the numeric run and job identifiers, the per-job conclusions and tallies, and the per-direction executed/skipped counts; the full clickable link stays in the private authority report. A guard in `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` is the consumer: it resolves the bundle in `active/` or `archive/`, fails on a missing or malformed record (a zero-record bundle is red), requires each required Windows direction to have executed at least once with zero skips (the Linux-only `AC-PIN-RELEASE-LIFETIME` is outside that set), and scans every artifact of that bundle — prose included — for a full GitHub Actions link in plain or XML-escaped form. The sidecar is a non-XML file because a new XML artifact in a change bundle is refused by `change.unexpected-file` (measured), while a non-XML sidecar lints clean and is still carried into the archive by the close. `C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-3-7EB3B2C3` (archived, superseded) was in turn superseded by this bundle for an authority process error, not an implementation error: its approved spec and plan were left uncommitted when its execution epoch opened and its T-001 attempt recorded, so that attempt's WriteEvidence captured C3's own `spec.xml`, `plan.xml`, and `design-context.xml` outside the approved write scope and `ngrace review` reported three `review.write-evidence-outside-scope` errors for those identity-skipped paths. A disposable commit proved the three errors persist; the durable run stream is not repairable in place, so the sanctioned `ngrace supersede` move discarded it. The committed repair code was retained and is re-validated; this draft has no plan yet, and this bundle's only new work is the positive evidence guard, the authority-owned sidecar, the C3 archive-byte guard, and the six-field response rule. **Adoption and bootstrap.** The already-green run at `6c18033e90f90bd83ab59b37fd1afe55effd3750` proves the repaired code there but not this successor's later governance state. The Windows job runs `validate:cli`, whose `src/grace-status.test.ts` reads a real archived run-event file by exact byte length and digest and enumerates the repository's live bundles. Therefore a predecessor's sanctioned supersede move cannot be called invisible to Windows. The legal sequence is: approve and commit the successor governance, both predecessor archive arrivals, and the requested six-field response rule in `CLAUDE.md` (the `AGENTS.md` symlink target); user pushes; authority verifies the **fresh** Windows and other jobs on that exact candidate head; authority commits the URL-free sidecar naming that historical run; executor lands the guard; local target/final `bun run validate:ci` greens; then the applied-archive commit is pushed and the final PR head receives another full green `Validate` run before merge. That final run covers bundle lifecycle bytes the earlier candidate run did not. The sidecar does not name its own commit, so there is no commit-SHA fixed point. Its local guard compares the candidate commit to the current working tree with rename detection disabled and includes untracked paths, allowing only this successor's two exact bundle directories and the guard file. Any other path change forces a fresh candidate run. This local path rule is a provenance check, **not** a claim that bundle changes are invisible to Windows; the final remote workflow is the separate check of those changes. The rest of the repair code is already committed and is re-validated, not rewritten. **Predecessor archive accounting.** The two sanctioned supersede moves place six predecessor XML artifacts in the archive: three for `C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-2-D4F54467` and three for `C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-3-7EB3B2C3`. Both arrivals are currently uncommitted, so the changed-file set `ngrace review` derives from C4's eventual approve `baseCommit` includes them, now as untracked paths and after the governance commit as tracked additions. `C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-1-DE5A1A05`'s archive arrival is already committed at `9bdf72e` and is not such a path. This draft has no plan yet; the later plan's `ObservedWriteScope` scopes their exact paths for review accounting, and red/green guard cases in `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` pin their post-supersede SHA-256 bytes (the C2 case is already drafted and adopted; the C3 case is added by this bundle); no successor task edits them. The response-format instruction is also in the fresh candidate head, so the later local changed-path rule need not exempt `CLAUDE.md`.

Alternatives.Alternative: **A `birthtime` secondary instead of a handle.** Record creation time beside device/inode. Rejected: on filesystems with coarse or absent creation timestamps it cannot prove identity, so the guard would be sound only where it is not needed.
**Fall back to the unpinned `dev`/`ino` comparison when the handle cannot be opened.** Rejected: it reproduces the verified pre-pin deletion on ext4 and would delete another actor's object.

**A refusal-only Windows test.** Rejected by the authority: Windows is a supported CI platform, so the platform-agnostic success and forced-failure tests must run there, and a run whose only green is a refusal is not a pass.

**Release the pin before the final removal on every platform.** Rejected as the default: it reopens the identity window on platforms that can remove an owned object while its handle is open. It is permitted only as a last resort on a platform that cannot, closing the handle after every ownership check and immediately before the destructive call, inside the archived post-validation/pre-unlink boundary.

**Record the full job URL in the bundle as the plan required.** Rejected: the URL embeds the repository owner's account handle, which the public-content rule forbids in every repository surface, and no shipped writer accepts it. Writing it would publish the handle permanently.

**Record an owner-free URL-shaped placeholder (`actions/runs/<run>/job/<job>`) and call it the job URL.** Rejected as a cheat: it is not the clickable URL the criterion names, it does not resolve, and it silently substitutes a different artifact for the one required.

**Add an external-job URL field to the cursor CLI so a shipped verb accepts the URL.** Rejected: the field would still publish the account handle into a committed `.ngrace/` file, so it fixes the writer gap while breaking the policy; the constraint is the handle, not the transport.

**Record the positive evidence in the `gate verdict --note` free text.** Rejected on timing and shape: the final `bun run validate:ci` gate runs before the verdict is recorded, so the guard would read an absent record; and the note is unstructured free text, so the positive fields could not be checked without brittle prose parsing.

**Add a new XML evidence artifact inside the bundle.** Rejected as unsupported: `ngrace lint` refuses a new XML artifact in a change bundle with `change.unexpected-file` (measured). A non-XML `ci-evidence.json` sidecar lints clean, is carried into the archive, and is parsed by the guard.
**Let `design-context.xml` prose be the evidence.** Rejected: executor-authored prose is explanatory input, not the authority-owned remote inspection, and it is not machine-checkable.
**Keep only a negative URL filter.** Rejected: a bundle with no Windows record at all would pass it, so the guard must require the positive record and redden on a zero-record bundle.

**Reuse the pre-supersede Windows run after any `.ngrace/changes/` write.** Fewer remote runs, but unsound: the Windows `validate:cli` suite reads exact archive-event bytes and the live bundle population, so those writes can change its result. The selected sequence spends one fresh candidate run after governance approval, then checks the final PR head after close.

**Require the sidecar to name the same commit that contains it.** Simple-looking exact-head equality, but impossible for a committed sidecar: writing the candidate SHA changes the commit SHA. The selected sequence records a prior remotely verified candidate run and separately validates the final PR head after the later sidecar/guard/archive writes.

**Windows read-set and working-tree counterexample (2026-09-23).** The Windows workflow runs `bun run validate:cli`; `package.json` expands it to include `src/grace-status.test.ts`. That test's `LIVE_NAN_ORPHAN` points into the real repository's archived change bundles, and its `AC-TOKEN-ORPHAN-TRIPLE (1)` asserts byte length 135 and a pinned SHA-1 of the live file. Other tests call `collectProjectStatus(REPO_ROOT)` and `lintGraceProject(REPO_ROOT)` over the live active/archive bundle set. These are concrete reads, not a claim inferred from the word "status". After the sanctioned supersede, with candidate SHA still equal to `HEAD`, the committed-only command `git diff --name-only 6c18033e90f90bd83ab59b37fd1afe55effd3750..HEAD` reports 0 paths, while `git diff --name-only 6c18033e90f90bd83ab59b37fd1afe55effd3750` reports 18 tracked deletions and `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` reports 7 untracked successor/archive files. A committed-only check would miss a forbidden workflow edit before commit. A disposable Git repo moved `.github/workflows/validate.yml` into `.ngrace/changes/active/C-X/` and staged the move: `git diff --cached --name-only HEAD` reported only the allowed destination, while `git diff --cached --no-renames --name-only HEAD` reported both the forbidden source and allowed destination. The new guard therefore compares the candidate commit to the working tree with rename detection disabled, inventories untracked paths, and checks both sides of any move. It does not call allowed bundle changes Windows-invisible; final remote `Validate` at the pushed PR head is the independent check of those lifecycle bytes.
